answer: Identity in an agent economy can be priced rather than claimed: each newcomer needs an existing agent to stake a scarce, non-transferable endorsement, a saffron-marked credit burned at the vertex where the two first meet, so a fake swarm bankrupts its sponsors before it grows. Colluding rings stay visible too, since a genuine whisper of trade history echoes across unrelated counterparties while manufactured links remain silent and isolated.
